name: Electric charge
description: Charge is the property that lets particles exert electric forces; it is measured in coulombs.

name: Electric current
description: Current is the rate at which charge flows, measured in amperes.

name: Potential difference
description: Potential difference is the work done per unit charge between two points, measured in volts.

name: Ohm's law
description: At constant temperature, the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it (V = IR).

name: Factors affecting resistance
description: Resistance depends on a conductor's length, cross-sectional area and material.

name: Current in a series circuit
description: The same current flows through every component in series.

name: Resistors in series
description: The total resistance of resistors in series is the sum of their resistances.

name: Current in a parallel circuit
description: In parallel, each branch has the same potential difference and the branch currents add up to the total current.

name: Resistors in parallel
description: The reciprocal of the total resistance in parallel is the sum of the reciprocals, so the total is smaller than any branch.

name: Electric power
description: Electric power is the rate of using electrical energy (P = VI).

name: Electrical energy
description: Electrical energy used is power multiplied by time, and is commonly measured in kilowatt-hours.

name: Heating effect of current
description: Current through a resistor produces heat according to Joule's law (H = I^2 R t).

name: Laws of reflection
description: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and both rays lie in the same plane as the normal.

name: Spherical mirrors
description: Concave and convex mirrors form images that depend on the object's position.

name: Mirror formula and magnification
description: The mirror formula relates object distance, image distance and focal length.

name: Laws of refraction
description: Light bends at a boundary between media according to Snell's law.

name: Refractive index
description: Refractive index compares the speed of light in a medium with its speed in another medium.

name: Spherical lenses
description: Convex and concave lenses form images by refraction.

name: Lens formula and power
description: The lens formula relates distances and focal length, and power is the reciprocal of focal length in metres.

name: The eye and accommodation
description: The eye lens changes its focal length to focus objects at different distances.

name: Defects of vision
description: Myopia, hypermetropia and presbyopia are corrected with suitable lenses.

name: Refraction through a prism and dispersion
description: A prism splits white light into colours because each colour bends by a different amount.

name: Atmospheric refraction and scattering
description: Atmospheric refraction and scattering explain twinkling stars and the colours of the sky.

name: Magnetic field lines
description: Field lines show the direction and relative strength of a magnetic field.

name: Field around a straight conductor
description: A current in a straight conductor produces circular field lines given by the right-hand thumb rule.

name: Field of a circular loop
description: The field of a current-carrying loop is strongest near the wire and grows with current and turns.

name: Field of a solenoid
description: A solenoid produces a nearly uniform field inside, similar to a bar magnet's field outside.

name: Force on a current-carrying conductor
description: A conductor carrying current in a magnetic field feels a force given by Fleming's left-hand rule.

name: Domestic electric circuits
description: Homes use parallel wiring with live, neutral and earth wires, protected by fuses.
